DDI sits mid-scale (3) as deepfake detectors exist but degrade against compression, re-encoding, and adversarial post-processing common on Shorts/Reels.

PCA is highest (5) because consumer-grade voice cloning APIs (ElevenLabs, OpenAI Voice) produce deployable audio for cents per minute, replacing hours of voice-actor labor. DDI is high (4) because audio deepfake detectors exist but degrade severely under codec compression, phone-channel transmission, and adversarial perturbation. AAS is mid (3) because podcast/audio platforms are largely format-neutral without the engagement-bait amplification dynamics of short-form video.

PCA is highest (5) because a single consumer API call to image generators like Midjourney or DALL-E produces deployable images in seconds, replacing hours of illustrator or photographer work at roughly 1/100 the cost. DDI sits at 3 because detectors like Hive and synthetic-image classifiers exist but degrade substantially under adversarial post-processing, compression, and inpainting. RCG is mid-range (3) because the EU AI Act and China's labeling law nominally cover synthetic images via disclosure requirements, but enforcement against the long tail of social-media images is minimal.

EDP is 4 given documented harms to search ecosystems, news credibility, and scientific record (paper mills), though most instances remain commerce/SEO rather than acute democratic-process damage.

DDI scores 3 because while detectors like SynthID and various CNN-based classifiers exist with reasonable in-domain performance, adversarial post-processing (JPEG compression, cropping, color grading) degrades detection substantially in realistic distribution.
